question.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ For all $q\in Z,$ ${q}^{2}$ is even.

choices.value: There exists $q\in Z$ such that ${q}^{2}$ is even.
There exists $q\in Z$ such that ${q}^{2}$ is not even.
For all $q\in Z,$ ${q}^{2}$ is not even.

current_example.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\qquad$ For all $n \in \mathbb{N},$ $n$ is a composite number.
current_example.worked_solution:
If we denote

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14257569/assets/6b623801f26e595ef6cc34036800888a5a3479798e354dde2547f61a94d1773d.svg)

our statement can be written as

$$
\forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \, P(n).
$$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\neg \left( \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \, P(n)  \right) \equiv \exists n \in \mathbb{N}, \, \neg P(n).
$$

Finally, $\exists n \in \mathbb{N}, \, \neg P(n)$ reads as follows:

$\qquad$ **There exists** $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $n$ is **not** a composite number.
